strings.name: Nancy Pelosi
strings.role: Politician · US representative · former House speaker
strings.summary: Pelosi entered Congress through Democratic organizing and has represented San Francisco since 1987. The first female House speaker in 2007, she returned to the role in 2019. She led House efforts on the Affordable Care Act, crisis relief, pandemic spending and climate legislation, alongside oversight and impeachment proceedings. She announced in 2025 that she would not seek reelection, but remained a representative through the term ending in 2027.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: The first female US House speaker, she played a role in major legislative processes on healthcare reform, budgets and congressional oversight.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Graduated from Trinity College in Washington, DC in 1962, studying political science; later worked in Democratic organizing.
strings.highlights.h1.title: First female House speaker
strings.highlights.h1.text: First elected in 2007 and returned to the speakership in 2019, after long leadership of House Democrats.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Organizing major legislation
strings.highlights.h2.text: Led House work on healthcare, pandemic relief, infrastructure, semiconductor and climate legislation.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Announced no reelection bid
strings.timeline.t1.text: Said she would not run in 2026 and would complete her existing term ending January 2027.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Ended second speakership period
strings.timeline.t2.text: Left the speakership after Republicans regained the House, remaining a representative and speaker emerita.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Advanced climate and semiconductor laws
strings.timeline.t3.text: Led House passage of the Inflation Reduction Act and CHIPS and Science Act, both collective legislative achievements.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Returned as speaker
strings.timeline.t4.text: Regained the role with the Democratic majority and later led the House through two Trump impeachments.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Advanced healthcare reform
strings.timeline.t5.text: Organized House passage of the Affordable Care Act, a central Obama-administration law.
strings.timeline.t6.title: First elected speaker
strings.timeline.t6.text: Became the first woman to hold the office, serving her first period until 2011.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Became House Democratic leader
strings.timeline.t7.text: Began two decades of leadership of the House Democratic caucus.
strings.timeline.t8.title: First elected to Congress
strings.timeline.t8.text: Entered the House through a special election, representing San Francisco.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Completed college
strings.timeline.t9.text: Graduated from Trinity College before developing a career in Democratic organizing and public affairs.
